questions.question: Your friend has been drinking and wants to drive. Which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Ask other friends to convince them not to drive.
Arrange another way for them to get home.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: You can prevent drunk driving by arranging other transportation, involving friends in activities to slow their drinking, and getting a group to intervene. But telling them to use less-crowded roads does not address the main problem.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should generally ride:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets the group stay close while giving each rider enough space to react safely. Switch to single-file when turning, going through curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may move back into your lane too soon.
You might block another vehicle from passing you.
The near side of the lane is safer.
You will feel more wind from the passing vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Staying on the far side of your lane may tempt the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes occur on trips under five miles long at speeds below 30 mph.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than those without helmets.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash, regardless of your speed.

questions.question: During the day, your headlight should:

options.text: Switch between high and low beam.

questions.explanation: Using your high beam during the day makes other drivers more likely to see you. Use high beam whenever you are not riding near or toward other vehicles.

questions.question: For eye or face shield protection to work well, it must have all of these features except:

options.text: Be too tight for sunglasses or eyeglasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be too tight for sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is safe for motorcyclists except when it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe for motorcyclists except when it rains.
questions.explanation: Oil drippings from cars create a strip in the middle of lanes. On dry roads, this area usually has enough traction for safe riding. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can often ride around it and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with arms fully stretched out.
Use arms to hold their body up.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms can control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see the roadway through vehicles in front of you.
When the weather is pleasant and clear.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions require longer stopping distances. This includes heavy traffic, poor weather, night riding, and when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What should you do to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on and ride in a lane position that helps other drivers see you. Maintain a safe space cushion. Do not assume that other drivers see you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: Why should you not change gears on railroad tracks?

options.text: Other drivers may not expect you to change gears.
The uneven surface makes it harder to switch gears.

questions.explanation: Do not shift gears while crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle might stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: Because of their small size, motorcycles appear to be:

options.text: Traveling faster than they actually are.
Traveling slower than they actually are.
Not moving when they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traveling faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's small size can make it look like it is traveling faster than it really is.

questions.question: If you carry a load in a sidecar, the stopping distance may:

options.text: Be the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Adding weight to your motorcycle increases its stopping distance. Start slowing and stopping earlier when carrying a load or passenger in the sidecar.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing suddenly. This alerts a tailgater following too closely that you are stopping for a hazard they may not have seen.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should always be avoided?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
No portion of the lane should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No portion of the lane should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best. Choose a lane position based on current riding conditions.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which factor does not affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed

questions.explanation: Three factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and food intake may also have an effect.

questions.question: Under ideal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Maintain a following distance of at least two seconds under normal conditions. Increase this distance whenever conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop far back, then slowly move forward.
Stop quickly right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance behind the vehicle in front of you, even when both are stopped. The other vehicle might back up without warning. You also need space to escape if another vehicle hits you from behind.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies some rear braking when the front brake is used.
Applies some front braking when the rear brake is used.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear brakes when either is used.
Records and remembers how hard the rider brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies some front braking when the rear brake is used.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system automatically applies some front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Check your motorcycle's owner's manual for details about your specific braking system.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the center of your lane.
Move to the left side of your lane.
Move to the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Staying too close to the passing vehicle increases the chance of a crash.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should less experienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without forcing the new rider to lead the group.

questions.question: How do you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Swerve toward the side with fewer hazards.
Press the brake and try to speed up.

questions.explanation: To regain control of a locked rear wheel, release the brake immediately. However, if the rear brake locks on a surface with good grip, you can keep it locked until the motorcycle stops.

questions.question: At minimum, how often should you check your motorcycle's hydraulic fluid?
questions.explanation: Check your hydraulic fluid and coolant at least once a week. Regular pre-ride inspections help keep your motorcycle safe.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Use headlights from vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: At night, use your high beam (unless meeting or following another vehicle), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective gear. Change your lane position as needed to see well, be seen, and stay safe.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Should be used to avoid hazards on slippery roads.

questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs lots of traction to work safely. Avoid sudden moves like swerving on slippery roads.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Do not swerve. Only use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do the actions one at a time, not together. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: When the road is wet, what part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.

questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks builds up in the center of the lane. This area usually has enough grip for motorcycles, but not when it is wet. The oil strip is usually narrow enough that you can ride beside it and still be in the center portion of the lane.
